lines.q: Welcome back, quiz friends! Grab a pen and keep score. Fifty questions from the nineteen sixties, from easy to legend. If you get forty right, your memory is excellent. Let's go! Which band was nicknamed the Fab Four?
lines.a: The Beatles! John, Paul, George and Ringo.

lines.q: Which city did the Beatles come from?
lines.a: Liverpool! The famous Cavern Club was their home stage.

lines.q: In nineteen sixty-one, which city was split in two by a wall?
lines.a: Berlin! The wall stood for twenty-eight years.

lines.q: Which country sent the first man into space, in nineteen sixty-one?
lines.a: The Soviet Union! Yuri Gagarin orbited the Earth once.

lines.q: Which famous doll got a boyfriend named Ken in nineteen sixty-one?
lines.a: Barbie! Ken was named after the inventor's son.

lines.q: Who gave the famous I Have a Dream speech in nineteen sixty-three?
lines.a: Martin Luther King Junior! In front of the Lincoln Memorial.

lines.q: Which nineteen sixty-nine music festival was held on a dairy farm in New York State?
lines.a: Woodstock! Over four hundred thousand people came.

lines.q: Which famous spy first hit cinemas in Doctor No, in nineteen sixty-two?
lines.a: James Bond! Played by Sean Connery.

lines.q: Which country won the nineteen sixty-six football World Cup?
lines.a: England! Their only World Cup win so far.

lines.q: Who said: float like a butterfly, sting like a bee?
lines.a: Muhammad Ali! Back then still called Cassius Clay.

lines.q: Now it gets a bit harder. Which mission first landed men on the Moon?
lines.a: Apollo eleven! In July nineteen sixty-nine.

lines.q: Which nineteen sixty-six TV show launched the starship Enterprise?
lines.a: Star Trek! To boldly go where no man has gone before.

lines.q: Who was the first woman in space?
lines.a: Valentina Tereshkova! In nineteen sixty-three. Sally Ride came twenty years later.

lines.q: Which British model was named The Face of sixty-six?
lines.a: Twiggy! She was only sixteen at the time.

lines.q: Designer Mary Quant made which fashion item famous?
lines.a: The miniskirt! Swinging London at its best.

lines.q: Who became US President after John F. Kennedy was killed?
lines.a: Lyndon B. Johnson! He was sworn in on Air Force One.

lines.q: Which nineteen sixty-two crisis nearly started a nuclear war?
lines.a: The Cuban Missile Crisis! Thirteen very tense days.

lines.q: Which band sang My Generation in nineteen sixty-five?
lines.a: The Who! Sneaky one, I know.

lines.q: Who played Mary Poppins in the nineteen sixty-four film?
lines.a: Julie Andrews! She won the Oscar for it.

lines.q: Which artist painted the famous soup can pictures in nineteen sixty-two?
lines.a: Andy Warhol! Thirty-two cans, one for every flavour. If you're enjoying this, subscribe and turn on the bell!

lines.q: Welcome to the hard round! Which nineteen sixty novel did Harper Lee write?
lines.a: To Kill a Mockingbird! It won the Pulitzer Prize.

lines.q: In which year did the Beatles first play The Ed Sullivan Show?
lines.a: Nineteen sixty-four! Around seventy-three million Americans watched.

lines.q: Who made the first ever spacewalk, in nineteen sixty-five?
lines.a: Alexei Leonov! Ed White was the first American, a few months later.

lines.q: In which year did Brasília become the capital of Brazil?
lines.a: Nineteen sixty! Built from scratch in about four years.

lines.q: Which Motown group was led by Diana Ross?
lines.a: The Supremes! Twelve number one hits in America.

lines.q: In which year did Concorde first fly?
lines.a: Nineteen sixty-nine! Passenger flights only began in seventy-six.

lines.q: Which nineteen sixties TV show starred a talking horse?
lines.a: Mister Ed! Of course, of course.

lines.q: Who was the British Prime Minister in the late nineteen sixties?
lines.a: Harold Wilson! From nineteen sixty-four to nineteen seventy.

lines.q: Which nineteen sixty-seven film features Mrs. Robinson?
lines.a: The Graduate! With a young Dustin Hoffman.

lines.q: Which ballet star defected to the West in nineteen sixty-one?
lines.a: Rudolf Nureyev! At a Paris airport. Baryshnikov followed in seventy-four.

lines.q: Now it gets really tough. Who sang A Whiter Shade of Pale in nineteen sixty-seven?
lines.a: Procol Harum! That organ line is unforgettable.

lines.q: Which nineteen sixty-two satellite first beamed live TV across the Atlantic?
lines.a: Telstar! It even got its own hit song.

lines.q: In which city was Martin Luther King killed, in nineteen sixty-eight?
lines.a: Memphis, Tennessee! Not Dallas, that was Kennedy.

lines.q: Who scored a hat-trick in the nineteen sixty-six World Cup final?
lines.a: Geoff Hurst! The first hat-trick ever scored in a World Cup final.

lines.q: Which US state was hit by the huge Good Friday earthquake of nineteen sixty-four?
lines.a: Alaska! Magnitude nine point two, the strongest ever recorded in North America.

lines.q: Which country had the world's first female prime minister, in nineteen sixty?
lines.a: Ceylon, today Sri Lanka! Sirimavo Bandaranaike. That one catches so many people.

lines.q: Who led the Soviet Union during the Cuban Missile Crisis?
lines.a: Nikita Khrushchev! Stalin had died almost ten years before.

lines.q: Which nineteen sixty-four Broadway musical has the song If I Were a Rich Man?
lines.a: Fiddler on the Roof! It ran for over three thousand shows.

lines.q: Which nineteen sixties puppet show featured International Rescue?
lines.a: Thunderbirds! Thunderbirds are go!

lines.q: Who wrote the nineteen sixty-two novel A Clockwork Orange?
lines.a: Anthony Burgess! Later a famous Stanley Kubrick film.

lines.q: Welcome to the legend round! Who managed the Beatles until nineteen sixty-seven?
lines.a: Brian Epstein! George Martin was their producer, not their manager.

lines.q: Which mission was the first to orbit the Moon, at Christmas nineteen sixty-eight?
lines.a: Apollo eight! They took the famous Earthrise photo.

lines.q: Who performed the first human heart transplant, in nineteen sixty-seven?
lines.a: Christiaan Barnard! In Cape Town, South Africa.

lines.q: Where did Cassius Clay win Olympic gold?
lines.a: Rome, nineteen sixty! He was only eighteen.

lines.q: Roughly how much money was taken in the Great Train Robbery of nineteen sixty-three?
lines.a: About two point six million pounds! A fortune in nineteen sixty-three.

lines.q: In nineteen sixty-five, Mariner four sent the first close-up photos of which planet?
lines.a: Mars! Just a handful of grainy pictures, but history.

lines.q: Which city hosted the nineteen sixty-eight Summer Olympics?
lines.a: Mexico City! The first Games in Latin America.

lines.q: Which band took its name from a Muddy Waters song?
lines.a: The Rolling Stones! From Rollin' Stone. Three left, stay with me!

lines.q: Who invented the computer mouse, first shown to the public in nineteen sixty-eight?
lines.a: Douglas Engelbart! It was made of wood.

lines.q: Last one. Who stayed in orbit around the Moon while Apollo eleven landed?
lines.a: Michael Collins! The loneliest man in history, some said.

outroLine: How many did you get? Comment your score below, and subscribe with the bell on for a new quiz every day!
